title: Reusable DTCG Runtime

scope.problem: RayX currently resolves design tokens through rayx_runtime_theming_dtcg, which mixes DTCG document resolution, RayX RuntimeTheme compilation, component token overrides, and loading assumptions. A reusable DTCG runtime is needed before RayX-specific theme integration can be simplified.
scope.outcome: RayX MUST contain a reusable, I/O-free dtcg_runtime crate under crates/rayx that resolves DTCG 2025.10 resolver JSON from already-loaded strings, supports lazy missing-document requests, applies deterministic token-path overlay semantics, resolves aliases across the full active graph, and projects requested token views into typed Rust structs without any RayX, gpux, GPUI, AssetService, filesystem, network, or async-runtime dependency.
inScope: Create crates/rayx/dtcg_runtime as the reusable DTCG resolver and projection crate.
Create a companion crates/rayx/dtcg_runtime_derive proc-macro crate only for derives and re-export it through dtcg_runtime.
Implement string-based document catalog APIs with logical ResourceId keys.

Implement resolver documents, token sets, modifiers, contexts, defaults, resolutionOrder, source arrays, references, fragments, groups, $root, $extends, effective types, token aliases, deterministic whole-token overlay, and bounded diagnostics for the DTCG 2025.10 contract.
Implement Resolution<T>::Ready and Resolution<T>::Missing so callers can provide referenced JSON from any external source.
Implement DtcgTokens projection, DtcgComponentTokens metadata, #[dtcg(rename)], #[dtcg(root)], #[dtcg(rest)], and TypeRegistry conversion keyed by Rust target TypeId plus effective DTCG $type.
Support narrow Rust target structs that expose only a strict subset of the active DTCG graph while unprojected tokens remain available for aliases used by projected tokens.

Add apps/test_suite routes and headed tests that visually display resolved generic DTCG token trees, context changes, missing requests, diagnostics, and typed projection output for manual exploration.
outOfScope: RayX theme publication, GPUI globals, whole-window refresh, AppBuilder extensions, AssetService adapters, packaged RayX theme assets, gpux converters, and RayxTheme definitions.
Filesystem, HTTP, URI fetching, ZIP loading, or asynchronous loading inside dtcg_runtime.
Generic Serde object merge or deep merge of Rust structs.
Deep merging composite token values; a later token at one token path replaces the complete previous token.
RayX legacy theming deletion; that belongs to the rayx-dtcg-theme-service epic.
DTCG drafts newer than the stable 2025.10 resolver contract.

actors.description: Provides resolver/source JSON strings, selects contexts, registers converters, and receives typed projected values or missing document requests.
Uses DocumentRequest values to load JSON by its own policy, then provides the text back to dtcg_runtime.
Defines Rust structs matching the DTCG hierarchy and derives projection metadata.
Uses apps/test_suite to inspect generic resolved token output and diagnostics visually.

functionalRequirements.title: Resolve DTCG 2025.10 documents deterministically
functionalRequirements.statement: dtcg_runtime MUST parse a 2025.10 resolver document and resolve sets, modifier contexts, defaults, resolutionOrder entries, source arrays, internal and external references, same-document JSON pointers, groups, $root tokens, required $extends semantics, effective token types, aliases, and token values into one deterministic semantic token tree.

behavior.trigger: A caller invokes resolve with a resolver resource and zero or more modifier-context selections.
outputs: Complete provenance for every winning token
stateChanges: Resolution caches record results for the current catalog revision and normalized context selection.
invariants: resolutionOrder and every sources array preserve declaration order.
A later token at the same token path replaces the entire earlier token.
Aliases resolve after overlay against the final winning token graph.
errors: Invalid resolver shape, invalid reference, invalid pointer, invalid group extension, alias cycle, missing alias target, conflicting type, unsupported construct, or broken alias used by a requested projection returns a structured DtcgError.
edgeCases: An omitted modifier selection uses its declared default.
A group containing $root maps both the group token and child tokens without name collision.
Reference sibling behavior follows DTCG reference rules and never becomes arbitrary JSON merge.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Conformance fixtures prove ordered set and modifier overlays, defaults, explicit contexts, source ordering, and whole-token last-wins replacement.
Fixtures prove internal and external fragments, relative references, aliases after overlay, alias cycles, inherited types, groups, $root, and required $extends behavior.
Repeated resolution of identical documents and normalized contexts produces byte-equivalent semantic output, provenance, request order, and fingerprint.

evidence.reason: The current workspace contains the resolver behavior that the generic crate replaces and generalizes.

provenance.userDecision: The user approved an independent generic dtcg_runtime with string provision, lazy Missing requests, DTCG overlay, typed converters, narrow projection, and visual test-suite coverage.

functionalRequirements.title: Keep loading outside the runtime
functionalRequirements.statement: dtcg_runtime MUST accept UTF-8 JSON strings through logical resource APIs and MUST NOT read a path, URL, AssetService, filesystem, network, or executor directly.

behavior.trigger: A caller creates a runtime or adds, replaces, removes, or batches documents.
inputs: Canonical or relative logical resource identifier
stateChanges: from_json, provide_json, provide_requested_json, provide_json_batch, replace_json, and remove_document update the in-memory catalog and invalidate caches.
invariants: The first document-provision argument is an opaque identifier and never path authority.
Relative identifiers canonicalize against the referring document identifier.
Fragments never participate in the catalog key.
errors: Malformed JSON, duplicate batch identifiers, invalid identifiers, request identity mismatch, or traversal above the logical root returns an error without partial batch mutation.
edgeCases: Application-owned catalogs can use names that resemble paths without granting filesystem semantics.
A root resolver can be supplied entirely from a string.
URL-like identifiers remain inert unless an external loader gives them meaning.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The crate exposes string-based root and document provision APIs and has no RayX, gpux, GPUI, async runtime, HTTP, or filesystem dependency.
Batch provision is atomic and resource replacement or removal increments one catalog revision and invalidates stale resolution results.
Resource identifier tests cover normalization, parent-relative resolution, fragment separation, traversal rejection, request identity, and already-loaded string ownership.

functionalRequirements.title: Request only the active document graph lazily
functionalRequirements.statement: Resolution MUST return Resolution::Ready(T) or Resolution::Missing(Vec<DocumentRequest>) and MUST request every currently missing document reachable from ordered sets and selected modifier contexts without requesting inactive modifier documents.

behavior.trigger: Resolution reaches one or more catalog resources that have not been provided.
outputs: Ready value after active documents exist
stateChanges: The runtime retains no hidden asynchronous operation; the caller provides text and invokes resolution again.
invariants: Each request contains canonical resource_id, referenced_from, and original_reference.
Unselected modifier contexts do not create ordinary requests.
The runtime returns all missing resources discoverable in the current pass.
errors: A reference cycle, invalid pointer, malformed newly provided document, or repeated no-progress missing frontier terminates with a structured error or stable Missing state instead of an infinite loop.
edgeCases: A newly provided document can reveal another missing level.
Several references to one resource produce one request with deterministic primary provenance.
validate_complete can enumerate inactive missing documents only when explicitly invoked.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A resolver with light and dark sources requests base plus only the selected or default theme source.
Providing requests one-by-one or as a batch converges to the same Ready value without runtime I/O.
Pending, recursive, duplicate, inactive, malformed, cyclic, and no-progress fixtures terminate deterministically with complete requests or structured errors.

evidence.reason: RayX already owns loading; the generic runtime must return missing-document requests instead of duplicating this authority.

functionalRequirements.title: Project typed views over the resolved graph
functionalRequirements.statement: #[derive(DtcgTokens)] MUST map a Rust struct hierarchy onto the resolved DTCG group hierarchy, treat the Rust target as a strict projected view over the active resolved graph, and use TypeRegistry converters keyed by Rust target TypeId and effective DTCG $type.

behavior.trigger: A caller resolves or projects a registered target T.
outputs: Fully initialized T with converted requested leaves
Unprojected resolved tokens retained for alias/reference resolution but absent from T
stateChanges: No partially initialized T is exposed.
invariants: Group nesting is the default mapping.
#[dtcg(rest)] collects registered unclaimed groups without inventing a JSON node.
Converters receive token value, effective type, path, and provenance.
Projection completeness applies to fields requested by T, not to every token present in the active graph.
errors: Missing required field, duplicate mapping, converter absence, target type mismatch, invalid converter output, unsupported token value, or broken alias used by a requested token returns a field- and token-qualified error.
edgeCases: A DTCG namespace such as spacing can be omitted from AppTheme while component-like projected tokens still resolve aliases to spacing tokens before projection.
A broken alias in an unprojected token is reported only by validate_complete or by a projected token depending on it.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A narrow AppTheme fixture exposes color fields while the active DTCG graph also contains spacing tokens and projection succeeds.
A projected component-like fixture resolves a dimension alias through an unprojected spacing namespace and receives the converted concrete value.
Rename, root, rest, required-field, unknown-converter, type-mismatch, unprojected-token tolerance, and broken-used-alias tests produce deterministic results with precise provenance.

evidence.reason: The current RayX-specific typed compiler demonstrates the projection responsibility that must become generic.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Cycle, depth, duplicate, input-order, cache invalidation, and deterministic-output stress tests pass.

risks: DTCG 2025.10 edge semantics for $ref siblings, $extends, $root, type inheritance, and external fragments can be implemented incorrectly without conformance fixtures tied to the normative contract.
A projection implementation can accidentally validate the whole active graph and reject legitimate internal reference-only namespaces unless narrow-target tests exist.
A diagnostic route inside apps/test_suite can accidentally become RayX-specific proof of runtime internals unless it consumes only public dtcg_runtime APIs.
Whole-graph alias resolution can become expensive without bounded walkers and baseline measurements.
deferredNonGoals: Dependency-granular invalidation and incremental alias recomputation after correctness is measured.
Built-in HTTP, filesystem, ZIP, or remote URI loaders.
RayX theme service, gpux converters, AssetService adapter, AppBuilder extension, and packaged theme assets.
Generic object overlay APIs unrelated to DTCG token-path semantics.
Graphical DTCG authoring, editing, persistence, or schema migration tooling.

compatibility: The crate targets the stable DTCG 2025.10 resolver contract and rejects unsupported constructs explicitly.
Sprint 1 public names become the compatibility boundary consumed by rayx_dtcg.
No compatibility facade for RuntimeTheme, GlobalTokens, or ComponentTokenStore exists in the generic crate.
publicApi: All document input APIs accept already-loaded UTF-8 JSON text paired with logical ResourceId values.
Resolution returns Ready, Missing, or structured DtcgError without hidden I/O.
Typed projection is opt-in and permits unprojected active tokens to satisfy aliases.
dependencies: dtcg_runtime and dtcg_runtime_derive contain no RayX, gpux, GPUI, AssetService, filesystem-loader, HTTP-client, or async-runtime dependency.
The proc-macro crate depends only on proc-macro support libraries and emits generic metadata.
data: A later active token at one token path replaces the complete earlier token.
Composite token values are never recursively deep-merged.
Resource identifiers are logical keys; fragments remain separate from catalog identity.
operations: The runtime performs no filesystem, network, or AssetService operations.
Implementation checkpoints use AgentX evidence, strict audits, and gitmaster commits limited to declared scope.
